baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the same four datum values, but Set A binds each value to the correct property name as labeled on the drawing ("finished floor elevation", "grade level elevation") and its quotes include the room label (KITCHEN/BEDROOM) that supports the entity binding. Set B renames the property as "finished floor height" and adds the condition "relative to grade level," an interpretation not stated on the sheet, while its grade-level quotes omit any room label, leaving the Kitchen/Bedroom binding unsupported. Set A is therefore the more faithful extraction, with no invented content.

variant-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the two level markers (GRADE LEVEL 0' - 0" and FINISHED FLOOR 2' - 9 1/2") as they appear in both the kitchen/dining section and the bedroom section, with values and quotes supported by the text layer. Set A additionally keeps the needed datum condition (finished floor relative to grade level), which the paired markers establish, whereas Set B labels the values as elevations without stating the datum. Neither set invents values or misbinds components, so the difference is small but favors A for retaining the condition.

baseline-first.note: Set A misbinds the elevation 2' - 9 1/2" to Grade Level, when the text layer clearly pairs that value with FINISHED FLOOR and gives GRADE LEVEL as 0' - 0". Set B correctly captures both datums for each section (C1 West Module and A1 East Module) with quotes matching the text layer. Set B also keeps the section/module conditions, while Set A's two claims are both wrong and redundant.

variant-first.note: Set A correctly separates the two datums — Finished Floor at 2' - 9 1 1/2"... i.e. 2' - 9 1/2" and Grade Level at 0' - 0" — and attributes each to both Section C1 (West Module) and Section A1 (East Module), with quotes that appear verbatim in the text layer. Set B misbinds the Finished Floor value (2' - 9 1/2") to Grade Level and its quote 'GRADE LEVEL 2' - 9 1/2"' does not exist in the source, so both of its claims are unsupported. baseline-first.note: Set B captures the key text values (KP(θ=0°)=0.0188 s, KI(θ=0°)=0.008068634, KD=0.0 s², ζφ=0.7), the GK(θ) formula and the KI(θ) formula of Eq. (7-19), plus consistent right-axis readings of the three curves. Set A systematically misreads the left axis as the gain axis (e.g. proportional gain 0.75/0.8/0.42/0.3/0.18 s and integral gain 0.3/0.18/0.12), and even invents K_P(θ=0°)=0.018182881 s, contradicting the stated 0.01882681 s. B is not flawless — it mixes axes for a few points (gain-correction 0.005 at 20°, 0.015 at 5°, integral gain 0.3/0.33 at 0°) and repeats several claims — but its errors are far fewer and it keeps the formulas and exact gains that A partly misses.

variant-first.note: Both sets mix correct text-derived values with chart readings, but Set A keeps the key stated facts intact (KP(θ=0)=0.01882681 s, KI(θ=0)=0.008068634, KD=0.0 s², ζφ=0.7, GK(θ)=1/(1+θ/θK), and the KI(θ) formula) and its figure readings are mostly plausible. Set B invents a KP value (0.018182881 s) not in the text, misstates the gains at θ=0 (0.020 s, 0.007, 0.005), and repeatedly binds left-axis gain-correction values (0.75, 0.42, 0.18, 0.3, 0.8, 0.12) to proportional/integral gains. Set A also has several left/right-axis confusions (0.8 s, 0.33, 0.3, 0.015, 0.005 at 20°) and some duplicated claims, but far fewer errors overall.

baseline-first.note: Both sets are factually accurate against Table 6-1: every value, unit and elevation/HtFract binding I checked in A and B matches the table rows (e.g., TwGJStif 472.75E+9 at 0.00 m, TMassDen 4550.87 kg/m at 26.28 m, TwFAIner 9958.2 kg•m at 52.56 m). The difference is in claim value: A spends 9 of its 25 claims on trivial entries (two bare 'Elevation' rows and seven 0.0 m cg-offset rows) and never captures a fore-aft stiffness value, while B covers TwFAStif plus more mass-density and inertia values with only 3 trivial claims. B therefore delivers broader, more informative coverage of the distributed tower properties at equal accuracy. Quotes in both are short but support the stated values.

variant-first.note: Both sets are numerically accurate against Table 6-1: every value, elevation and HtFract I checked matches the corresponding row and column, so neither set misbinds or invents data. Set A covers a broader mix of properties (mass density, fore-aft/side-to-side inertia, stiffnesses) with fuller quotes, while Set B devotes 7 of its 25 claims to trivial facts (five identical 0.0 m cg-offset entries and two bare elevation entries) and several quotes give only the bare value with no row context. Set A therefore delivers more useful, well-supported claims at the same claim count, with only 3 trivial entries versus B's 7.

baseline-first.note: Set A is internally clean — every wiring-schedule claim (marks 10, 20, 31, 32, 33, 34, 50, 150 and the AL feeder to the main service panel) is correctly bound and quoted — but it ignores the entire NOTES block, so it misses the 120/240V 1-phase 3-wire sub-panel, the 50A/2P main breaker, the 2.8kW inverter with ground fault, the 60A DC NFDS, the 200A/2P NFDS and the NEMA 3R junction box. Set B captures those equipment ratings and the sub-panel voltage in addition to the same wiring-schedule data, with only one clear defect: the Component 6 rating is misread as '200/2 A/P' instead of 200A/2P. B also duplicates some rows (Circuit/Wiring pairs), but its coverage of the page's key engineering facts outweighs A's omission of all equipment ratings.

variant-first.note: A captures the NOTES equipment facts — 120/240 V sub-panel, 2.8 kW inverter with ground fault, 60 A DC NFDS, 200 A/2P NFDS, NEMA 3R junction box — which B omits entirely, while both parse the wiring schedule rows (20/31/32/33/34/50/150/151/10) correctly. B is padded with trivial per-row restatements (e.g. "conductor material CU") and mislabels the AL 3#4/0, #4G., 2-1/2"C. row as the "Main Service Panel connection," although the run to the main service panel is circuit 50 (CU 3#6, #8G., 1"C.). A makes that same misbinding in three vague "PV Equipment wiring … to main service panel" claims, plus assigns the ARMORED CABLE row to 150 (it is 151) and garbles 200A/2P as "200/2 A/P". On balance A's coverage of the important rated values outweighs its extra errors.

baseline-first.note: Both sets are heavily redundant, repeating the same two figure annotations (∂P/∂θ(θ=0) = -25.52E+6 watt/rad and θk = 6.302336°) and the doubling relation, and both include the same unsupported graph-read estimates (e.g., -90E+6 at the 'last data point', which the figure shows near -120E+6). Set A binds the values to the NREL 5-MW baseline wind turbine, matching the text, whereas Set B repeatedly misbinds them to 'Blade-Pitch Controller' and 'Rotor-Collective Blade-Pitch' (the x-axis variable), which are not the component owning pitch sensitivity. Set A's main defects are calling θk an 'intercept' and a couple of rough plot estimates; Set B has about six misbound-entity claims on top of the same bad estimate, so A is the more faithful set.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the page's key annotated values (∂P/∂θ at θ=0 = -25.52E+6 watt/rad, θK = 6.302336°, and the doubling relation of Eq. 7-17) and both repeat them redundantly, and both share the same bad graph estimate of -90E+6 at the last data point (the point near 23° is about -115E+6). Set B adds two clear misreadings of the text: it labels ∂P/∂θ(θ=0) as the "slope" and θK as the "intercept" of the best-fit line, whereas the page says the slope and intercept are the two bracketed terms of Eq. (7-16a) and θK is a blade-pitch angle where sensitivity has doubled. Set A avoids those mislabels and keeps the θK and rated-point values correctly bound, though it loosely attributes several turbine quantities to the "Blade-Pitch Controller" and uses the legend entry "Original Data" as a quote that does not support its plotted-value claims. Overall A is somewhat more faithful, with fewer substantive misreads.

baseline-first.note: Both sets extract the same two figure values (∂P/∂θ at θ=0 = -25.52E+6 watt/rad and θK = 6.302336º) and both contain redundant duplicate claims. Set A invents a 'Blade-Pitch Controller' entity that appears nowhere on the page and binds pitch sensitivity to the blade-pitch axis rather than the turbine/power quantity. Set B correctly attributes the regression results to the NREL 5-MW baseline wind turbine named in the text, but mislabels θK = 6.302336º as the 'best-fit line intercept' when the text defines θK as the blade-pitch angle where pitch sensitivity has doubled (the intercept is ∂P/∂θ at θ=0).

variant-first.note: Set A correctly binds the -25.52E+6 watt/rad pitch sensitivity at θ=0º to the NREL 5-MW baseline wind turbine named in the text, and keeps the θ=0º condition. Set B invents a 'Blade-Pitch Controller' entity not present on the page and misattributes both values to it or to 'Rotor-Collective Blade-Pitch' rather than the turbine's pitch sensitivity. However, Set A also errs by labeling 6.302336º as the best-fit line intercept (it is θK, the blade-pitch angle where pitch sensitivity doubles) and includes a vague bare 'θ' claim; Set B likewise treats 6.302336º as a generic angle. Both sets duplicate claims and truncate the unit to 'watt/ra' in one claim, but A's entity bindings are more faithful overall.

baseline-first.note: Both sets bind values to the correct components and properties with supporting quotes, and both contain some redundancy (e.g., brake torque and rotor speed listed twice from prose and table). Set A additionally captures the DOWEC turbine power loss of 0.35 MW with its rated-power and 6.25 MW aerodynamic power conditions, an important fact Set B omits. Set A also binds the generator efficiency and gearbox frictional-loss assumption to the NREL 5-MW baseline turbine more explicitly, while Set B's 'gearbox | frictional losses' entity is slightly less specific. Neither set contains misread or invented values.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the core drivetrain values with faithful quotes and correct units, and both contain harmless duplicates (brake torque, gearbox ratio, rotor speed). Set B additionally captures the DOWEC turbine's 0.35 MW power loss with its rated-power and 6.25 MW aerodynamic-power conditions, a real fact from the text that Set A omits. Set B's only weakness is looser entity binding on three claims (generator efficiency, driveshaft damping constant, gearbox frictional losses attributed to the NREL 5-MW turbine rather than the component), but the attribute names the component so these are not misreadings. Neither set invents values.

baseline-first.note: Both sets share the same core correct claims (HabEx 4 m/4 instruments/52 m starshade, LUVOIR-A 15 m/4, LUVOIR-B 8 m/3, Lynx 3 m/3, Origins 5.9 m) and the same fragment-entity errors ('axis telescope', 'n-axis telescope', 'spacecraft', 'baseline mission concept/spacecraft') plus a mislabeled 10 m 'size/dimension' for the grazing incidence mirror assembly. Set B does extract 'Lynx | focal length | 10 m' correctly and keeps the 'flying in formation' condition on the starshade, giving it better coverage of the page's facts. Set B carries one extra mislabeled 10 m claim, so the wrong counts are nearly even, but its correct focal-length claim tips the balance.

variant-first.note: Both sets are heavily duplicated and contain garbled entities ('axis telescope', 'n-axis telescope', 'spacecraft', 'baseline mission concept') that misbind instrument counts, and both wrongly treat Lynx's 10 m as a mirror-assembly 'size/dimension' rather than focal length. Set A additionally captures the correct Lynx focal length of 10 m and the starshade 'flying in formation' condition, which Set B never states correctly. Set B's coverage is otherwise similar but it omits the focal length fact entirely and adds an invented condition ('spacecraft with starshade') on a vague claim. Overall A is slightly more complete and faithful despite one extra low-quality claim.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the same core facts (grade level 0'-0", finished floor 2'-9 1/2", and 3/8" = 1'-0" scales), but Set B binds the elevations to the named sections (Section - East/West Module) and its quotes include both the finished floor and grade level lines, supporting the 'relative to grade level' condition. Set A adds several redundant and vaguer claims (e.g. 'building | grade level', 'West Module | grade level', and duplicate Grade Level/Finished Floor elevation entries) without adding new information. Neither set invents values, but Set B is more precise and less padded.

variant-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the grade level datum at 0' - 0" and the finished floor at 2' - 9 1/2" above grade for both the West and East Module sections, with quotes that support the values. Set B additionally captures the drawing scale (3/8" = 1'-0") for both section views, which Set A omits entirely. Set B's only weakness is one vague claim binding grade level to a generic 'building' entity, while Set A is clean but redundant and missing the scale facts. Overall B covers more of the page's engineering content with comparable accuracy.

baseline-first.note: Both sets contain duplicate claims for KP, KI, KD and the damping ratio, but Set B's duplicates consistently bind the values to the baseline blade-pitch controller as stated in the text and figure caption. Set B also keeps the meaningful condition that ζφ = 0.7 is the upper limit of the recommended range used to compensate for neglecting negative damping from the generator-torque controller. Set A instead has one claim whose 'condition' is merely the symbol zeta_phi, which is vague and adds nothing, and it omits the compensating rationale. Otherwise the numeric values and quotes are identical and correct in both sets.

variant-first.note: Both sets contain the same four core facts (KP, KI, KD at θ = 0º and ζφ = 0.7), each duplicated with only cosmetic entity-name variants, so neither adds real coverage. Set A's damping-ratio claim keeps the meaningful condition (used to compensate for neglecting negative damping from the generator-torque controller), which is directly supported by the text. Set B instead offers a claim whose 'condition' is merely the symbol name (zeta_phi), which is trivial and misuses the condition field. Otherwise the values, units and quotes are faithful in both sets.

baseline-first.note: Set B captures the key facts cleanly — hub height 150 m, 10-m monopile diameter, 120-m blades, 20–30 m clearance range from the footnote, and the Table 4-1 steel/soil values — with only a few chart-range guesses and one invented 'steady-state' condition. Set A repeats many claims and introduces several clear errors: density given as 785E3 kg/m^5 and 785E3 kg/m^3, shear modulus as 793E3 Pa, a 0.18 Hz tower frequency contradicting the stated 0.170 Hz, a 0.0 Hz Kaimal peak, soil shear modulus misbound to the Tower, and 'ground height 30 m' misreading clearance. B does omit the soil Poisson's ratio of 0.4 and its 1P/3P band readings are approximate, but its errors are far fewer.

variant-first.note: Set A binds the Table 4-1 values correctly (E=200E11 Pa, G=7.93E10 Pa, rho=7.85E3 kg/m3, Gs=140E6 Pa) and captures the hub height, 10-m monopile diameter, 30-m clearance, 100-t transition piece and 0.170 Hz mode, but it repeats several claims and gives two mutually contradictory, chart-inconsistent 1P ranges (0.09–0.13 Hz and 0.12–0.25 Hz) plus an invented 'steady-state' condition. Set B adds the soil Poisson's ratio of 0.4 that A misses, but it misreads table entries (785E3 kg/m^5, 785E3 kg/m^3, 793E3 Pa), reports 0.18 Hz alongside 0.17/0.170 Hz, and includes vague or misbound claims such as 'ground | height | 30 m' and 'Tower | Shear modulus, soil'. Overall A has fewer outright wrong or unsupported claims despite its duplication.

baseline-first.note: Set B binds the same dimension strings to the correct detail entities (Module A and Module B PV structural members), capturing the overall lengths 12'-3 3/4" and 10'-3 3/4" and the L3X3X1/4 member profiles, which Set A leaves as vague 'PV Detail' dimensions. Both sets repeat the 3/8" through-bolt and L3X3X1/4 claims and both attach the S-301 reference as a condition, so those issues cancel out.

variant-first.note: Set A captures the key engineering facts visible in the details: the Module A and B overall lengths (12'-3 3/4" and 10'-3 3/4"), the L3X3X1/4 angle profiles, and the 3/8" through bolt, all supported by the drawing. A's only clear error is the Module A bolt claim of 5/16" (the sheet shows 5/8" values and 3/8" through bolts, never 5/16"), while B's 6" claim is vague and unbound. Overall A is substantially more complete and faithful despite one misread value.

baseline-first.note: Set A covers the key dimensional facts on the page — the 2'-9 1/2" finished-floor elevation and the 18'-0" solar-envelope height — which Set B omits entirely, while both capture the material callouts correctly. Set B pads its list with three redundant duplicates (handrail 2x4 cedar stated three times, cladding twice, the APSE-20 tube array twice) and a vague 'flatbar | material | steel' claim, adding trivial claims without adding information. Set A's only defect is binding the 18'-0" solar envelope height to 'finished floor to solar envelope' when the drawing labels it as an elevation above grade level (0'-0"). Overall A is more complete and more faithful.

variant-first.note: Set A repeats the same handrail and cladding material claims several times and includes a vague bare 'flatbar | material | steel' claim, while omitting the elevation dimensions entirely. Set B is more compact and captures the finished-floor-to-grade dimension (2'-9 1/2") correctly. However, B misbinds 18'-0" as a finished-floor-to-solar-envelope height, whereas the drawing labels it as the solar envelope elevation above grade level. Despite that one misbinding, B's coverage of the height facts and lack of redundant claims make it the stronger set.

baseline-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the Cooking thresholds (full points ≥80 oz/2300 g, reduced 16–80 oz, no points ≤16 oz/450 g) and the 96.00 oz (2.721 kg) starting-water minimum, and both repeat many of these facts redundantly. Set A additionally covers the Dinner Party facts (two parties per team, 0–100% score range), which Set B omits entirely, so A has better coverage of the page. Set B invents a '100 points per cooking task' value not stated anywhere and asserts 0 points for vaporized weight < 80 oz, which contradicts the figure, plus it splices quotes ('5.000 lb vaporized', 'the starting water weight sha'). Set A's errors are mainly quote problems (caption used as support for the 0-point rule, a garbled 'sh[all be]' quote) and one misbinding of the 0–100% range to the final score rather than the percentage integer scores.

variant-first.note: Both sets cover the Cooking thresholds thoroughly but are highly redundant; Set A additionally contains a clear misread (0 points for vaporized weight < 80 oz, when the figure gives 0 points only at ≤16 oz) and an unsupported 100-points claim whose quote is only the figure caption, plus an altered quote for the 5.000 lb reduced-points bound. Set B's errors are milder (a caption-only quote for the 0-point threshold, a garbled reconstructed quote, and the 0–100% range loosely bound to the dinner-party final score rather than the percentage integer scores). Set B also captures Dinner Party facts (two parties per team, 0–100% scoring) that Set A omits entirely, so B is the more complete and faithful set.

baseline-first.note: Set B correctly binds all 15 table rows to the sensitivity of aerodynamic power to blade pitch (∂P/∂θ) with the full row conditions (wind speed, rotor speed, pitch angle) and supporting quotes. Set A attributes every value to a 'Baseline Blade-Pitch Controller' entity that does not appear anywhere on the page, and it fragments rows into partial claims that drop the pitch-angle and rotor-speed conditions, leaving values ambiguously bound. Set A also omits several ∂P/∂θ and pitch-angle values while adding trivial standalone wind-speed claims. B is complete, faithful and condition-preserving; A is largely misbound and incomplete.

variant-first.note: Set A extracts all 15 rows of Table 7-1 with correct values, units, and full conditions (wind speed, rotor speed, pitch angle), each supported by a quote matching the table. Set B misattributes every claim to a 'Baseline Blade-Pitch Controller' entity that does not appear on this page (the table concerns sensitivity of aerodynamic power to blade pitch), and it fragments the table into trivial single-cell claims (e.g., wind speed or rotor speed alone) while omitting most ∂P/∂θ values and the rotor-speed condition. Set A is complete and faithful; Set B is largely misbound and incomplete.

baseline-first.note: Both sets extract the same five legend entries from Figure 2-11 (pitch axis, mass center, neutral center, geometric center, shear center) as chordwise-position structural properties of the blade, with essentially identical binding and quotes. Neither captures any numeric values or units from the mass density, stiffness, or axial stiffness plots in Figure 2-10, and both are equally limited to trivial legend labels. Set A's attribute wording ('structural property center') is marginally more specific than Set B's, but this does not change correctness. The sets are effectively equivalent.

variant-first.note: Both sets extract the same five legend entries from Figure 2-11 (pitch axis, mass center, neutral center, geometric center, shear center) as chordwise-position structural properties of the blade, with quotes that match the text layer. Neither set captures any numeric values, units, or the mass-density/stiffness data in Figure 2-10, so both are equally limited to trivial legend labels. Set B's attribute wording ('structural property center') is slightly awkward but not misbound relative to Set A's ('structural property'). No claims in either set are misread or invented.

baseline-first.note: Both sets contain one fabricated damping claim (edgewise 5% with an altered quote '3%, 5%, and 6%'), but Set A otherwise binds the damping values (3%, 3%, 6%), the s-coordinate endpoints (0 at suction-side TE, 1 at pressure-side TE), and the flatback trailing-edge definition correctly. Set B additionally misbinds several figure labels as blade 'components' (Plane of Rotation, Pitch Axis, Chord Line) and garbles the flatback trailing-edge definition into a claim about the flatback surface. Set A also keeps the flatback trailing-edge definition as a proper definition claim, while B duplicates the s-coordinate and damping facts without adding correct content.

variant-first.note: Both sets hallucinate the same non-existent quote '3%, 5%, and 6%' and therefore both report the first edgewise damping as 5% when the page states 3%, 3%, 6% for flapwise, edgewise and torsional. Set A adds further problems: it misbinds the flatback rule (the trailing edge, not the normalized arc length position, is defined as the midpoint of the flatback surface) and repeats the damping and s-coordinate claims several times. Set B keeps the flatback trailing-edge definition correctly bound and includes the s = 0 / s = 1 figure annotations with clear conditions, with less duplication. Set B is therefore the cleaner and more faithful set, though both share the same damping error.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the same core drivetrain values with supporting table quotes, but Set A repeats the rated rotor speed three times (two redundant/trivial claims) and binds the brake time constant to the high-speed shaft rather than the brake. Set B keeps the fully-deployed condition on the brake torque and has only one redundant rotor claim, while still covering all nine table properties. Set B is thus slightly cleaner and more faithful, with no invented values in either set.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the nine Table 5-1 values with supporting quotes, but each pads the list with duplicate rotor-speed claims (A two, B three). B additionally misbinds the brake time constant to the 'High-Speed Shaft' rather than the brake, and drops the fully-deployed condition on the brake torque that A keeps. B does retain 'rated' conditions on the rotor and generator speeds, but its extra duplicate and misbound entity make A the cleaner set.

baseline-first.note: Both sets are heavily duplicated and largely faithful to Eqs. (7-6) through (7-10), but Set A's claims are consistently bound to the right quantities with correct formulas and conditions. Set B introduces errors: one PID claim drops the derivative dot (ΔΩ instead of ΔΩ̇), one claim mislabels the T_Gen formula as a 'relationship to low-speed shaft rotational speed', and one vague claim ('negligible variation') is trivial with a bracketed, non-verbatim quote. Set A's only weaknesses are truncated quote fragments, which do not change the claim content.

variant-first.note: Both sets extract essentially the same four relations (Eqs. 7-6 through 7-10) with heavy internal duplication, and both bind the values to the right quantities with the Region 3 / Taylor-expansion / PID conditions kept. Set A adds the correct definition of θ (full-span rotor-collective blade-pitch angle), but it also contains a PID variant whose value drops the derivative dot (K_D N_Gear ΔΩ instead of ΔΩ̇) and two quotes stitched together with a bracketed '[torque]' substitution rather than verbatim text. Set B's formulas are consistently faithful but it omits the θ definition, garbles one PID value (ΔẊ_Ω) and has two truncated quotes ('on 3 is…', 'generator sp'). Net differences are minor and offsetting.

Set A correctly captures the distributed Table 6-1 properties (mass density, fore-aft/side-to-side/torsional/axial stiffness, inertias) with values bound to the right Elevation/HtFract rows and quotes that support them, plus the geometry, taper, mass and mass-center facts. Set B omits every table entry and instead repeats six claims (effective density, integrated mass, thickness scaling, Young's modulus, mass center, typical density), which are redundant rather than new evidence. B's one advantage is the shear modulus (80.8 GPa), which A misses; A's only quibble is restating the 30% thickness increase as a '1.3 ratio'.

baseline-first.note: Set B correctly binds the Table 6-1 distributed properties (mass density, fore-aft/side-to-side stiffness and inertia, torsional and axial stiffness) to the right elevations and column headers, with units and elevation/HtFract conditions matching the table, while also covering the narrative facts (dimensions, moduli, densities, taper, mass, mass center). Set A gets the narrative values right but omits the entire distributed-property table, the main quantitative content of the page, and repeats six claims (effective density, Young's modulus, thickness scaling, integrated mass, typical density, mass center) as near-duplicates. B's only notable defect is restating the 30% thickness increase as a "1.3 ratio," a value not stated in the document; B also omits the 80.8 GPa shear modulus that A captures.

variant-first.note: Both sets are padded with duplicated diagram-label component claims, but B captures the key numeric spec — the wire's 15C–30C transformation temperature range — that A omits entirely, and B also correctly derives materials (aluminum louvers/frame, nylon bearing sleeve, ABS parts) and the 3-Axis-CNC mill. A uniquely captures two behavioral facts (contraction on heating, added strain lowering the transition temperature), but its first quote is mangled ('rotates a assembly') and it never states the temperature range. Each set also misbinds a whole-assembly count (250 louvers or 32 rods) to a single 'Screen Assembly', so their error counts are comparable; B's better coverage of the page's quantitative and material facts gives it the edge.

baseline-first.note: Set B captures the key behavioral facts from the prose — the Flexinol wire contracts on heating to rotate the idler pulley, Kevlar strings transfer that rotation to the pulleys, and added strain lowers the transition temperature — all correctly bound with their conditions, whereas Set A omits these entirely and offers only the 15–30 C range (itself quoted as "transition temperature" rather than the text's "transformation temperature range"). Both sets pad heavily with trivial diagram-label component claims and duplicates, but A has more of them (about 16 versus 12). B's defects are quote-fidelity slips ("rotates a assembly", "cutting of each of the 250 louvers") and one misbound condition (32 rods tagged "final assembly" rather than the pulley assembly), while B's only important omission is the 15–30 C transformation range that A does state.

variant-first.note: Set A correctly captures several spanwise values from the plots — twist ≈15° at r/R=0 and ≈0° at r/R=1, chord ≈5 m at the root, and prebend ≈0 m at the root — whereas Set B returns nothing and misses every fact in Figure 2-4. However, A misreads the relative thickness curve badly (claims 21% at the root where the curve is ≈100%, and 15% at the tip where it is ≈21%) and gives 25% pitch-axis chord location at both ends when the plot shows ≈50% at the root and ≈37% at the tip (25% is off-scale). A also drops the sign on tip prebend (−4 m, claimed as +4 m), and its tip chord ≈1 m is only approximate for a steep end drop. Despite roughly half its claims being wrong, A's correct extractions still outweigh B's complete omission.

baseline-first.note: Set A contains no claims at all, so it captures none of the spanwise quantities plotted in Figure 2-4. Set B correctly binds chord, twist, prebend, relative thickness and pitch-axis chord location to the blade with the right r/R conditions and units, and gets the root chord (~5 m) and root twist (~15 deg) right. However, B misreads several endpoints: relative thickness is 100% at the root and ~21% at the tip (not 21% and 15%), pitch-axis chord location is 50% at the root and ~37% at the tip (not 25% at both), prebend at the tip is about -4 m (sign lost), and tip chord/twist are ~1.5 m and ~-1.5 deg rather than 1 m and 0 deg. Despite these errors, B's correct extractions and full coverage of the plotted quantities outweigh A's empty output.
